findings.requirement: Current owner consistency at graph/policy/Legacy integration; work items 1.2/1.5 and AC09-11
findings.observed: A real Legacy DRAFT has flexible_workflow_plan.created_by but no execution_policy/authority_target. Another owner can create a graph with that ID because change checks only those two ownership sources. The original creator's later Guard.confirm is rejected by the newly added foreign graph owner check.
findings.consequence: Unauthorized cross-owner reservation of an existing plan ID blocks legitimate guarded execution, with no normal graph deletion recovery for that creator.
findings.minimal_resolution: Before graph insertion/adoption, under the same authority lock transaction also validate the existing flexible_workflow_plan.created_by against the current owner's actual actor, preserving the established Guard.confirm creator semantics. Reject foreign Legacy ownership even without policy/target.
findings.evidence: Actual GraphPlans.change, Guard.confirm, WorkflowPlanService.draft and JDBC insert trace; no runtime reproduction.

findings.requirement: Preserve authoritative Delivery/WorkspaceResult contract; work items 1.4/1.5 and AC11
findings.observed: SoftwareDelivery uses List.equals for changed files. Existing Guard.validateResult uses HashSet equality and WorkspaceResult normalizes to TreeSet order. Delivery [b.py,a.py] and actual [a.py,b.py] are legitimately accepted and hashed but then shown as CONFLICT.
findings.consequence: A valid completed final result can be falsely reported as conflicting delivery evidence.
findings.minimal_resolution: Use the same file-set equivalence or shared normalization as the authoritative completion contract, retaining raw digest and all task/version/source checks without rewriting Delivery history.
findings.evidence: Static comparison of the new view with actual validateResult and WorkspaceResult constructors.
